Regulation: B.C. Reg. 143/2026
Made under: Residential Tenancy Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 23, 2026

B.C. Reg. 143/2026, deposited July 23, 2026, under theRESIDENTIAL TENANCY ACT[section 97]. Order in Council 356/2026, approved and ordered July 23, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that, effective July 30, 2026, the attached Residential Tenancy (Supportive Housing) Regulation is made. — C. BOYLE,Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs; N. SHARMA,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. RESIDENTIAL TENANCY(SUPPORTIVE HOUSING) REGULATION 1In this regulation,"Act"means theResidential Tenancy Act. 2In this regulation,"landlord","residential property","tenancy agreement"and"tenant"have the same meaning as in section 4.1 (1)[interpretation and application: supportive housing]of the Act. Supportive housing rental units –  prescribed matters 3(1)	In this section,"support worker"means an employee of a supportive housing operator whose duties include providing housing stability support. (2)	For the purposes of the definition of "supportive housing operator" in section 1 of the Act, the following persons or organizations are prescribed: (a)	the British Columbia Housing Management Commission; (b)	the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; (c)	a municipality or regional district; (d)	a corporation incorporated by, or in which shares have been acquired by, a municipality or regional district for a purpose that includes providing affordable housing; (f)	a board within the meaning of theHealth Authorities Act; (g)	a society within the meaning of theSocieties Act; (h)	a corporation within the meaning of theCanada Not-for-profit Corporations Act; (i)	a registered charity within the meaning of section 248 (1) of theIncome Tax Act(Canada). (3)	For the purposes of the definition of "housing stability support" in section 1 of the Act, a housing stability support that meets all of the following criteria is prescribed: (a)	the support must be available on the premises of the residential property on which the supportive housing rental unit is located; (b)	the support must be provided by a support worker;

minutes_briefs.title: BC creates new rules for supportive housing tenancies under the Residential Tenancy Act
minutes_briefs.summary: BC has made a new regulation under the Residential Tenancy Act that sets out who counts as a 'supportive housing operator' and what counts as 'housing stability support' (on-site help from a support worker to keep tenants housed). The regulation lists the types of organizations that qualify as operators, such as BC Housing, CMHC, municipalities, health authorities, societies, non-profits and registered charities. It took effect July 30, 2026.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you operate supportive housing, confirm you meet the new operator and on-site support worker definitions, and update your tenancy agreements and practices to match.
